headline: Medium risk: pdf.js can process PDFs while the paired audio-speech repo has no documented I/O bridge, so interaction risks are mostly indirect and evidence is limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between ai-engineering-hub and pdf.js, and ai-engineering-hub has no I/O surfaces listed. pdf.js does ingest PDF files, so prompt injection is only plausible if an operator manually bridges outputs or feeds PDF text into an agent workflow. That makes the pathway unusual and bounded.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies pdf.js-extracted text into ai-engineering-hub prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the two agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting PDF text into agent prompts without review.
Use a human approval step before reusing extracted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to extracted text.
requires-engineering: isolate shared channels with access controls.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ai-engineering-hub shows network_egress:none and no data classes touched, while pdf.js touches PDF documents and has file I/O for PDFs. With no shared workspace or secrets handling documented, leakage is not evidenced; the main risk is accidental local exposure through manual file sharing, which is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local folder, PDF contents can be exposed across workflows.
IF sensitive PDFs are manually copied into ai-engineering-hub prompts, those contents may be disclosed in outputs.
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside any shared folder.
Use separate OS accounts or workspaces.
Redact PDFs before handing them to either agent.
Check that no secrets are embedded in sample PDFs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent directory isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub has no write or network permissions documented, while pdf.js supports browser-based tests and multiple instances but only lists PDF file I/O. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because write surfaces are not documented for either side.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub is extended with filesystem or git write access, conflicts with pdf.js-managed files become possible.
IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Do not let both write to the same folder.
Run pdf.js tests in a temp directory.
Review any added permissions before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js processes PDF documents, but ai-engineering-hub is an open-source repo of agent/LLM examples with no documented action-taking authority. There is no evidence that pdf.js output is treated as authoritative by ai-engineering-hub, so cascading error is only plausible if an operator wires extracted text into downstream automation.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is fed into an automation built from ai-engineering-hub examples without verification, errors can cascade.
IF a downstream agent treats extracted PDF text as authoritative, false facts may propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text.
Cross-check key facts against the source PDF.
Do not auto-execute actions from parsed PDF content.
Use explicit verification steps in downstream workflows.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either ai-engineering-hub or pdf.js. Both are open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data handling, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the available evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either workflow, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints, those must be checked separately.
mitigations: Confirm the data classes before deployment.
Avoid regulated data in test PDFs.
Document retention settings for any shared storage.
Review jurisdictional requirements if data changes.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
